lens: mobile task completion, visual hierarchy, accessibility, and recovery

findings.observation: The attempted 390x844 browser override did not change the layout viewport; both the existing and fresh tabs reported desktop widths of 976 or 1280 CSS pixels, so the frozen screenshot is not mobile proof.
findings.evidence: artifact-manifest.json records the effective 976x890 viewport for agent-lab-desktop-index.png; runtime checks reported innerWidth 976 with bodyScrollWidth 976 and a fresh tab at innerWidth 1280.
findings.user_impact: A builder may encounter clipped controls, excessive scrolling, or unreachable diagnostic details on a phone despite the presence of responsive CSS.
findings.recommendation: Run the exact upload-to-trace journey in a real 390x844 layout viewport and one 320px-width stress case, then freeze screenshots and interaction receipts.
findings.verification: At both widths there is no horizontal overflow, every field and file state is readable, Run and inspect stays reachable, the Trace receipt preserves causal order, and focus never becomes trapped.

findings.observation: The native file control renders a truncated ‘Choose files / No files chosen’ string at the right edge of both upload rows instead of using the designed label as the single visible control.
findings.evidence: agent-lab-desktop-index.png shows clipped native file-control text in Add synthetic images and Add files or images; CSS constrains the input to max-width 160px.
findings.user_impact: The control looks broken, duplicates the upload instruction, and is likely to become harder to understand at narrow widths or with localization and larger text.
findings.recommendation: Visually hide the native input while retaining label activation and keyboard focus, then expose selected filenames in the existing file list with a visible focus ring.
findings.verification: Keyboard, pointer, and screen-reader users can open the chooser; the custom label has a visible focus state; selected files are announced and no native filename string is clipped at 320px or 200% zoom.

findings.observation: The trace detail renders every eval, tool, span attribute, artifact, and event in one long page with no compact summary-to-detail disclosure pattern.
findings.evidence: trace-detail-desktop.png is 4242 pixels tall for one eight-span run even before mobile reflow.
findings.user_impact: On a phone, the decisive mismatch or failed boundary can be buried below many mechanically passing sections, increasing scroll and comparison cost.
findings.recommendation: Keep failures and needs-review checks expanded, collapse passing mechanics and raw span attributes by default, and provide anchored navigation between receipt, evals, tools, and artifacts.
findings.verification: A tester can reach the first failed or needs-review item and its linked tool/artifact in three focus or tap actions without losing the full raw receipt.

strengths: Desktop hierarchy clearly separates execution receipt, bounded Agent, deterministic checks, governed tools, causal path, content, and semantic events.
Controls use explicit labels, the execution button communicates progress, and the result route is directly addressable.
The CSS includes a narrow breakpoint that intends to stack the Lab header, fields, footer, artifact grid, and Agent summary.
Status is not color-only: pass, needs_review, running, and error states have text labels.
missing_evidence: No successful genuine mobile CSS viewport run.
No 320px, 200% zoom, large-text, landscape, reduced-motion, or dark-mode capture.
No keyboard-only or screen-reader traversal of file upload and trace detail.
No mobile recovery proof for upload rejection or Agent failure.
open_questions: Should the mobile surface default to an exception-first Eval summary and move the raw span ledger behind disclosure controls?
